title: Pull the evidence
briefing: Before/after the outage, you want web-01's application log on ops-01 so you
can analyze it here (and keep a copy).
Copy /var/log/app.log off web-01 to your home directory with scp.
tips: scp copies over ssh. A remote path is written host:path — e.g. admin@web-01:/var/log/app.log.
`scp admin@web-01:/var/log/app.log ~/` downloads it into your home dir.
objective: Copy /var/log/app.log from web-01 to your home directory on ops-01 (so ~/app.log exists locally).
hints: scp takes a remote source and a local destination: `scp admin@web-01:/var/log/app.log <dest>`.
Send it to your home directory: `scp admin@web-01:/var/log/app.log ~/`.
`scp admin@web-01:/var/log/app.log ~/`, then `cat ~/app.log` to read it locally.
explanation: scp is ssh's file-copy cousin: host:path means 'on that machine', a plain path means local. Pulling logs down to analyze them (or pushing a fixed config up) is daily work — same auth, same hosts as ssh.
